items.item_text: American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross Basic Life Support (BLS), or UC Davis Health CPR
Minimum 1 year of direct patient care
Work experience in a customer service-related field
Hospital-based work experience

The Hospital Assistant 2 (Per-Diem) supports the delivery of rehabilitation services within the Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) at UC Davis Health. Working under the supervision and direction of licensed Physical Therapists and Occupational Therapists, the Hospital Assistant provides direct and indirect patient care support, assists with patient mobility and treatment activities, and helps maintain a safe, organized, and efficient clinical environment.
70% - Assists therapists with patient treatment and patient care activities for routine patients, as directed by a therapist from a predetermined therapy treatment plan

The position supports daily rehabilitation operations by preparing treatment areas, cleaning and maintaining equipment, monitoring inventory, and assisting with ordering and restocking clinical and office supplies. Additional responsibilities may include assisting with patient restraint procedures, supporting staff and student training related to mask and Powered Air-Purifying Respirator (PAPR) fit testing, and learning to assist Speech Pathologists with patient care procedures, as appropriate.
10% - Provides Support and Staff Training

As an important member of the rehabilitation team, the Hospital Assistant works collaboratively with clinical staff to support efficient workflows, patient safety, and a positive care experience. The role requires strong communication and organizational skills, attention to detail, adaptability, and a commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.
10% - Miscellaneous Assignments as Required
5% - Miscellaneous and Housekeeping
5% - Provides primary and backup services for ordering system
Must see well enough to observe patient reactions and read relevant monitors, relevant device settings, and relevant written information
Must hear and speak well enough to communicate with patients and staff throughout the day
Must possess the physical strength to assist with patient mobility
Basic knowledge in Occupational, Speech, and Physical Therapy
Effective leadership and team-building skills
Verbal and written communication skills to effectively communicate with hospital staff in a clear, concise, professional manner
Knowledge of or ability to learn appropriate information required for patient and supply record-keeping
Skill in organizing written material
Ability to handle challenging situations with sound judgment, adaptability, and professionalism.
Ability to exercise tact and diplomacy
Ability to offer guidance and accept constructive criticism professionally
Knowledge of and skill in using Microsoft Outlook, Excel, and Word, along with basic computer proficiency and the ability to quickly learn new computer programs and systems
